claims.text: Definition: new-onset AF w.in 30 days after surg, picked up by ECG (a single recording or 24-h monitoring).
claims.quote: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF), delineated as the emergence of new-onset AF within a 30-day timeframe after surgery, is typically identified through the application of electrocardiography (ECG) techniques, encompassing either a single recording or a comprehensive 24-h monitoring session

claims.text: Incidence after ⍉cardiac surg: 2% to 30%, peaking 2–4 days after surg.
claims.quote: The occurrence of POAF following NCS demonstrates a wide-ranging incidence rate, spanning from 2% to 30%, with a peak manifestation typically observed within 2–4 days postoperatively

claims.text: Often silent: in one study 83% of pts w post-op AF were aSx.
claims.quote: Higuchi et al. reported that 83% of patients with postoperative AF were asymptomatic

claims.text: ⍉benign: POAF carries a higher risk of CVA, MI and death than ⍉POAF.
claims.quote: patients with POAF face an increased risk of stroke, myocardial infarction, and mortality compared to their counterparts without POAF

claims.text: Watch closely: the elderly, obese, and pts w CVD, COPD or OSA (esp men).
claims.quote: Anesthesiologists should exercise particular vigilance when dealing with the elderly, obese, or those with preoperative comorbidities like cardiovascular disease, COPD, and OSAS, especially male patients.

claims.text: Perioperative factors to monitor closely incl serum potassium, serum magnesium, ♡ US and inflam factors.
claims.quote: Perioperative risk factors, including serum potassium, serum magnesium, cardiac ultrasound, and inflammatory factors, should be closely monitored

claims.text: Mgnt: rhythm control (pharm or electrical cardioversion) or rate control w BBs, nondihydropyridine CCBs and/or digoxin.
claims.quote: Uncontrolled POAF can be managed using either a rhythm or rate control strategy. A rhythm control strategy is aimed to achieve conversion to sinus rhythm via pharmacological or electrical cardioversion. In contrast, a rate control strategy is aimed to lower the ventricular heart rate of atrial fibrillation (AF) using β-blockers, nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, and/or digoxin.

claims.text: It = unclear whether rhythm or rate control = better for uncontrolled POAF.
claims.quote: It is unclear whether one strategy is superior to the other for managing uncontrolled POAF.
